---
title: "Teaching"
description: "Behavioural economics and health economics at the University of Newcastle."
---

I teach behavioural economics and health economics. The courses use current
research rather than textbook summaries of it, and each one makes students handle
data at some point, because the gap between reading a coefficient and producing
one is where the understanding is.

## Open teaching material

Some behavioural economics material is public, including the
[certainty effect](/blog/posts/why-99-does-not-feel-like-100/) explainer and its
recorded webinar. Use it in your own teaching if it is useful; attribution is
appreciated and permission is not required.
